newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Teck Wah says 1997 outlook is flat.
newsitem.headline: Teck Wah says 1997 outlook is flat.

text.p: Teck Wah Paper Products Ltd's 1997 financial performance was not expected to show significant improvement over 1996, when net profits plunged 98 percent, the company said on Tuesday.
"The directors expect some improvements in the overseas subsidiaries this year, but overall group performance is not expected to be significantly better than last year," it said in a statement.
The company said its results were affected by start-up costs at its Indonesian unit and continued loss-making at its China operation.
Other factors affecting the result included weak demand, a drop in selling prices and a rise in operating expenses.
Net profit plummeted to Singapore $49,000 for the year to December 31, 1996 from S$2.1 million in 1995.
Teck Wah's 1996 annual dividend of four percent was half of 1995's eight percent payout to shareholders.
